_note: Sensors YOU have explicitly claimed. Receiving a sensor is NOT owning it, so nothing appears here by inference alone -- the code will never add an entry for you. Anything not listed is reported as third-party and gets no label, no history, and no alert.
_how_to_identify_your_own: Run the tpms315 or ism433 lane, then drive your own vehicle in and out of range.
Your own tyre sensors show up as a tight group with near-identical sighting counts and a much higher SNR than passing traffic (on the author's station, 19.8-22.4 dB against 8-14 dB for the street).
Confirm it deliberately. A high SNR is evidence, not proof, and a neighbour parked closer than the road will outrank a car going past.

Do not add a sensor you merely suspect is yours. See docs/COVERAGE.md: a sensor id identifies a device, never a person, and labelling someone else's device as though you know whose it is is the exact mistake this file exists to prevent.
_vehicles_note: Group claimed sensors into vehicles so the console can report one line per car instead of four per tyre. Presence is stated honestly: 'parked' is inferred from TPMS going quiet when stationary, which is a property of the sensor, not a claim that anybody is home.
